model_literal_scan.scope: Source, configs, Compose templates, CI and scripts; ignored live credentials, data and third-party model names cited in historical research.
model_literal_scan.status: no concrete model IDs used as defaults

issues_found_during_live_validation: Provider could ignore native JSON Schema while returning syntactically valid JSON; new structured stages now also describe their schema in the prompt.
Natural-language term matching and repeated background could hide a tail answer; tokenize configured lexical terms and distribute evidence by distinct matches.
Widened excerpt windows could exceed the per-context cap; enforce the actual character allocation.
Citation label presentation brackets caused strict anchor lookup failures; normalize one label without changing its identity, and continue rejecting unknown labels and invented quotes.
Audit intermediate-fact instructions and their schema used inconsistent field names; align the contract and validate exact visible quotes.
validation_limits: Isolated Docker containers used the existing env credentials and temporary synthetic source artifacts.
The live smokes validate knowledge compilation and query-chain integration; binary document parser quality, production data and real image inference were not live-tested.
Image snapshot immutability, source offsets, table paging, collection fact visibility and both lexical backends are covered by offline tests.
The two live workloads differ because only the SQLite run compiled knowledge; their latencies are not a backend performance A/B.
No claim of general accuracy improvement; a held-out corpus and human checks are still needed.
Rebuild the running application to use the new code and re-ingest old documents to add derived node questions, aliases and summaries.
